items.review_rationale: Reviewed the minimum of Krull dimensions across every open neighbourhood of x; this differs from the dimension of the closure of x or a dimension based on just one arbitrary open.

references.context: Topology: open subset of ambient space containing specified point x

references.disposition: The definition takes a minimum of the dimensions in the stated collection, not an arbitrary neighbourhood value.

items.review_rationale: Read the entire universal scheme fibre-product property with projections commuting over S and a bijection for all test schemes T. Kept the equal-composite requirement and universal uniqueness.

references.phrase: universal pair of maps T→X, T→Y over S
references.context: Algebraic geometry: representing compatible pairs of S-scheme morphisms by maps into a fibre product

references.phrase: morphisms correspond bijectively for every T
references.disposition: Both existence and uniqueness are required, not merely a square with commuting projections.

items.review_rationale: Read local affine-neighbourhood requirement for a locally ringed space, including isomorphism with the prime spectrum equipped with its structure sheaf; no single global affine presentation is asserted.

references.context: Algebraic geometry: sheaf of commutative rings on prime spectrum of R
Algebraic geometry: invertible locally ringed space morphism preserving structure sheaves and local stalks

references.phrase: every point has an open affine neighbourhood
references.disposition: Local affine charts are required, but the whole scheme need not be affine.

items.review_rationale: Read all parts of a scheme morphism: continuous underlying map, compatible map of structure sheaves in the contravariant direction, and induced local homomorphisms of stalks.

references.phrase: locally ringed spaces X and Y

references.context: Sheaf theory: morphism of sheaves on Y into pushforward of a sheaf on X
Commutative algebra and sheaf theory: induced maps on stalks of structure sheaves preserving maximal ideals

references.disposition: The sheaf map reverses the direction of the underlying continuous map; no ordinary covariant map O_X→O_Y is inferred.
